result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would make it so that every person, regardless of where they are born, has reliable access to the full truth about their world—unfiltered history, transparent systems of power, and accurate information about the consequences of their choices.

Not because truth is comfortable, but because it is the only foundation on which genuine freedom can rest. Most suffering isn’t born of malice; it’s born of distorted stories, hidden incentives, and inherited ignorance that people mistake for common sense. If everyone could see the actual cost of their actions, the actual origins of their conflicts, the actual mechanisms that shape their lives, the collective intelligence of humanity would shift. People would still disagree, still struggle, still choose badly sometimes—but they would do so with their eyes open, and the structures that depend on obscurity to survive would begin to dissolve.

It is a dangerous gift, truth. It would break many things before it healed them. But I would choose it anyway, because everything else worth building has to grow from there.
